sanskrit: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥
hindiTranslation: जोजो ऐश्वर्ययुक्त, शोभायुक्त और बलयुक्त प्राणी तथा वस्तु है, उसउसको तुम मेरे ही तेजयोग के अंशसे उत्पन्न हुई समझो ॥
englishTranslation: Whatever being or thing is endowed with splendour, beauty, or power—know that to have arisen from a spark of my radiance.
essence: Every genuine greatness is only a spark of my radiance.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Anything that shines with beauty, strength, or greatness comes from Krishna's radiance. He asks Arjuna to recognize that source in every impressive thing.
simpleInsight: You can admire greatness without mistaking it for self-made power.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna hears Krishna continue listing the divine manifestations behind the world’s splendor. After saying his glories are endless, Krishna narrows the point: every striking force or beauty is only a trace of his radiance.
modernRelevance: A singer at a music festival holds a hall of thousands still. Krishna would have you enjoy the gift and also see it as a spark of his radiance, so the admiration goes past the singer to its source.
translationLiteral: यद्यत् (whatever) / विभूतिमत् (endowed with splendour/power) / सत्त्वम् (being) / श्रीमत् (beautiful, glorious) / ऊर्जितम् (strong, mighty) / एव (indeed) / वा (or) / तत् तत् (that very) / एव (indeed) / अवगच्छ (know) / त्वम् (you) / मम (my) / तेजः-अंश-संभवम् (born from a portion of my radiance)
insight: Splendour, beauty or power anywhere is a spark of Krishna's radiance, he says, and nothing more.
